speaker_role: independent counselors (Moon Prep counselors Nicole and Kieran; Nicole describes prior experience as a high school guidance counselor)
commercial_incentive: yes; Moon Prep is a paid admissions counseling business and repeatedly references 'your Moon Prep counselor' and paid passion-project services
key_insights: Debunks 'this is the essay that got me into [school]' viral posts, noting essays are read holistically alongside test scores/extracurriculars, so a single essay's causal impact can't be isolated or verified
Warns against trusting Reddit admissions rumors (e.g., interview invite timing), which are often years out of date or unverifiable; recommends checking official program websites and portals instead

Debunks 'my school only lets in X students' myths, explaining these usually stem from misunderstood macro-level quota systems (e.g., UNC Chapel Hill's county-based quota) rather than individual school caps

Debunks the 'colleges want well-rounded applicants' myth, describing a roughly decade-long shift toward valuing depth and authentic passion in a narrower set of activities over broad, shallow involvement

Debunks viral 'I earned $X million in scholarships' posts, explaining these typically sum small annual awards across dozens of separate school acceptances over four years each, none collectible simultaneously since a student attends only one school

Recommends applying where your stats sit at the top of the admitted range specifically when merit scholarship money is a priority, since colleges use aid strategically to win over top-of-pool applicants
notable_or_distinctive: directly debunks several currently-circulating TikTok/Reddit-era admissions myths with named specific examples (UNC Chapel Hill's county quota, '$1.5 million in scholarships' posts) rather than only older generic myths
reliability_notes: presenters are paid counselors who promote their own passion-project service partway through; myth-debunking claims are asserted from professional experience rather than cited data, though broadly consistent with mainstream counseling consensus
